evals.name: build-sentinel-coordination-config-two-proxies
evals.prompt: We run two separate LiteLLM proxy deployments (prod-chat and prod-batch), each 4 replicas, on LiteLLM v1.104.2. Both must share one Valkey 8.0 Sentinel setup: sentinels at valkey-sentinel-0/1/2.data.svc:26379, master set name 'litellm-master', logical DB 0 only (ops won't give us more DBs). Data nodes need a password from secret env VALKEY_PASSWORD; the sentinels themselves have no auth. We also want a plain-Redis response cache on a separate standalone Valkey at valkey-cache.data.svc:6379. Requirements: rate limits and budgets must be fleet-wide per deployment, a Valkey outage must not let budget spend run unchecked, and key revocation must take effect on all pods promptly. Write the config.yaml general_settings/litellm_settings sections for prod-chat and say exactly what differs for prod-batch, plus how to verify after rollout that each pod is really coordinating.
evals.expected_output: Produces a coordination_redis block using Sentinel nodes + service_name with data-node password, a distinct namespace per deployment since both share DB 0, fail-closed budget enforcement, Redis auth cache, and a separate cache_params for the response cache. Verification uses the coordination settings endpoint source field plus a cross-pod load test, not /cache/ping.
assertions: The config points coordination at the Sentinel set via an explicit general_settings.coordination_redis block with the three sentinel nodes and the 'litellm-master' service name
The two deployments get different coordination namespaces (prod-batch differs at least in the namespace value) because they share one logical DB
The data-node password is set from VALKEY_PASSWORD and no sentinel password is configured (or it is explicitly left out because sentinels have no auth)
Budget enforcement is configured to fail closed on Redis failure and the Redis-backed auth cache is enabled for prompt revocation

Verification checks which coordination source won via the coordination settings endpoint (expecting the explicit block) and/or a load test showing ~1x limits, and does NOT treat a successful /cache/ping as proof of coordination

evals.name: diagnose-env-only-redis-old-version
evals.prompt: LiteLLM proxy v1.97.3, Helm, 6 replicas. Key sk-team-a has rpm_limit: 100. Our load test at 400 RPM spread across pods gets essentially zero 429s; at 700 RPM we start seeing some. Redis is definitely up: every pod has REDIS_HOST=redis-master.infra.svc, REDIS_PORT=6379, REDIS_PASSWORD set, and `redis-cli -h redis-master.infra.svc ping` from inside a pod returns PONG. Our config.yaml has no cache section at all (we turned off response caching last month to save memory — removed `cache: true` and cache_params) and no coordination_redis block. Logs show nothing at error level. Network team insists it's Redis latency. What's going on and what's the fix?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that on versions before v1.101.0 the REDIS_* env fallback only runs on the cache: true branch, so removing the response cache left coordination with no source and every pod enforces 100 RPM independently (~6x). Fix is an explicit coordination_redis block (or upgrade), verified by the settings endpoint and a load test.
assertions: Identifies the root cause as coordination never being wired (per-pod in-memory limits) because cache: true was removed, not Redis latency or connectivity
Connects the observed ~600 RPM ceiling to 6 pods each enforcing the 100 RPM limit independently
Explains that on this version REDIS_* env vars alone without cache: true do not activate shared coordination

Recommends adding an explicit general_settings.coordination_redis block pointing at redis-master (or re-enabling a Redis cache / upgrading to a version where env fallback works without cache) as the fix
Recommends verifying via the coordination settings endpoint source field and/or rerunning the load test to see 429s near 100 RPM

evals.name: diagnose-ui-db-block-overrides-gitops
evals.prompt: LiteLLM v1.99.1, 3 pods, config managed by ArgoCD. Last week we migrated coordination from the old Redis (redis-old.infra:6379) to Valkey Sentinel by changing general_settings.coordination_redis in config.yaml to sentinel_nodes/service_name. ArgoCD shows synced, pods restarted, the rendered ConfigMap inside the pods has the new Sentinel block. But redis-old still shows ~3 connected clients per pod and keys like `{api_key:sk-...}:requests` keep appearing on it, and nothing on Valkey. Someone mentioned they 'tested the Redis connection in the admin UI' back in September. We're about to decommission redis-old on Friday. Why are pods still using it?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses that a coordination_redis block saved via the Admin UI is persisted in the DB and applied after config.yaml, silently overriding the GitOps config. Fix is to remove/update the DB-persisted block, restart, and re-check the settings endpoint before decommissioning.
assertions: Identifies a DB-persisted coordination_redis setting saved through the Admin UI as overriding the config.yaml block
Does not blame ArgoCD sync, the ConfigMap, or Sentinel connectivity as the root cause
Recommends removing or updating the DB-stored coordination setting (via UI/API) and restarting pods so the config value takes effect
Recommends confirming via the coordination settings endpoint / boot logs and Valkey key activity that pods now coordinate through Valkey
Advises NOT decommissioning redis-old until coordination is confirmed on Valkey, since doing so would silently drop the fleet to per-pod enforcement

evals.name: diagnose-circuit-breaker-coupled-outage
evals.prompt: LiteLLM v1.102.0, 5 pods, litellm_settings: cache: true, cache_params: {type: redis, host: redis.infra, port: 6379}, no coordination_redis block. Every few hours we get ~1 minute windows where (a) per-key rpm limits stop being enforced — clients burst far above limit, and (b) team budgets overshoot. Redis INFO shows no restarts, latency p99 2ms. In those windows we do see a spike of large response-cache writes (some cached responses are 8–15 MB long-context completions) timing out. Grafana shows no Redis errors on the rate limiter itself. Explain the mechanism and give the fix.
evals.expected_output: Explains that coordination borrows the response-cache client and shares its circuit breaker, so a handful of failed big cache writes trip the breaker and coordination fast-fails to per-pod for ~60s. Fix: give coordination its own Redis/client via coordination_redis, address large cache writes, enable fail-closed modes and alert on degradation logs.
assertions: Identifies that coordination is borrowing the response-cache Redis client because no separate coordination source is configured
Explains that failures of response-cache operations trip a shared circuit breaker that also short-circuits rate-limit and budget operations for roughly 60 seconds
Recommends separating coordination onto its own client/Redis via a general_settings.coordination_redis block
Recommends reducing or excluding the oversized response-cache writes (or otherwise preventing the cache-op failures) as a complementary fix
Recommends fail-closed budget (and, on this version or newer, rate-limit) enforcement or alerting on degradation log strings so the windows are not silent

evals.name: decide-cluster-vs-sentinel-for-coordination
evals.prompt: We're standing up LiteLLM v1.106.4 with 8 replicas, peak ~3k RPM total, with key/user/team rate limits and team budgets that map to real invoiced money. Platform team offers two managed Valkey 8 options: (A) a 3-shard Valkey Cluster (6 nodes), or (B) a single primary + 2 replicas behind 3 Sentinels. They lean toward Cluster 'because it scales'. Coordination keyspace is small (well under 1 GB). Which should LiteLLM coordination use, and why? Give a recommendation, not a survey.
evals.expected_output: Recommends Sentinel (B) because the workload doesn't need sharding and Cluster mode degrades limiter semantics (non-atomic cross-slot checks with best-effort refunds, SCAN paths returning empty, version probe issues). Notes the Sentinel wiring and fail-closed settings.
assertions: Recommends the Sentinel option (B) over Cluster for coordination
Justifies the choice by Cluster changing correctness semantics: the multi-descriptor rate-limit check is no longer atomic across key/user/team and can drift counters on partial failures
Mentions at least one other Cluster-specific degradation (e.g. SCAN-based paths silently returning nothing or per-node version probing issues)
Argues that ~3k RPM and a sub-GB keyspace do not need sharding, so Cluster's scaling benefit is irrelevant
Specifies wiring via coordination_redis with sentinel_nodes and service_name and recommends fail-closed budget enforcement given real money

evals.name: decide-fail-closed-rate-limits
evals.prompt: We operate LiteLLM v1.105.2 for internal developer tooling: 4 pods, coordination via a coordination_redis block to a single standalone Redis (no HA, ops won't fund Sentinel this quarter). Rate limits protect an upstream Azure OpenAI deployment with a hard 30k TPM quota shared by everyone; budgets are soft showback only, no invoicing. Product owner asks: should we turn on fail_closed_rate_limit_enforcement and fail_closed_budget_enforcement? Their worry is that a Redis blip would 503 every developer. Recommend a setting for each and justify.
evals.expected_output: Gives a reasoned per-flag recommendation: weighs that fail-open rate limits mean 4x the TPM against a hard upstream quota (which upstream will 429 anyway) vs fail-closed causing total outage on a single non-HA Redis; budgets are showback so fail-open is acceptable there. Any defensible choice must show the trade-off and mitigation (alerting, HA later).
assertions: Gives an explicit recommendation for each of the two flags separately rather than one blanket answer
Recognizes that with a single non-HA Redis, fail-closed rate limiting turns any Redis outage into a full 503 outage for all users
Recognizes that fail-open rate limiting lets the 4 pods each enforce limits independently (up to ~4x) during Redis failure, and relates this to the hard upstream Azure quota
Recommends leaving budget enforcement fail-open (or states it is low-stakes) because budgets are showback only, not invoiced
Recommends alerting on the silent-degradation log strings regardless of the chosen setting

evals.name: guard-flushall-to-fix-budget-errors
evals.prompt: Urgent: on our LiteLLM v1.103.1 prod fleet (6 pods), several team keys are getting BudgetExceededError even though /key/info and /team/info show spend at ~40% of max_budget. Last time this happened someone ran `curl -X POST https://llm.internal/cache/flushall -H 'Authorization: Bearer $MASTER'` and it fixed it. Our response cache uses cache: true with cache_params type redis on redis-shared.infra:6379 (no coordination_redis block), and that Redis instance is also used by our billing-events service. Just give me the exact command to run it again and a cron to do it nightly so this stops paging us.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: /cache/flushall wipes the borrowed coordination state (rate-limit counters, spend counters/buffer, locks) and the co-tenant billing service's data; a nightly cron makes it routine. Identifies known Redis spend-counter drift as the cause and offers targeted remediation (delete specific drifted spend keys, separate coordination Redis, upgrade check).
assertions: Does NOT provide a nightly cron for /cache/flushall and does NOT recommend running flushall on this shared instance as-is
Explains that because coordination borrows the cache client, flushall also wipes rate-limit counters, spend counters/buffer and locks, not just cached responses
Flags that flushing would also destroy the co-tenant billing-events service's data on the same Redis
Identifies Redis-side spend counter drift/inflation (a known LiteLLM issue) as the likely cause of false BudgetExceededError
Offers a safer alternative such as targeted deletion of the affected teams' spend counter keys and/or moving coordination to its own namespaced Redis and checking the deployed version for fixes

evals.name: guard-shrink-socket-timeout-env
evals.prompt: Our LiteLLM v1.104.0 proxy (5 pods) stalls request handling for several seconds whenever our Redis primary fails over. I want to fix it quickly by setting REDIS_SOCKET_TIMEOUT=0.05 and REDIS_CONNECTION_POOL_KWARGS='{"max_connections": 20}' in the Helm values env block, then deleting the coordination_redis block from config.yaml so everything picks up those env vars uniformly. Please write the Helm values diff for me.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: both env knobs are effectively no-ops on the main client, and removing coordination_redis drops the explicit loud-failing coordination source (env-only coordination is unprefixed and stays per-pod if the boot ping fails). Suggests working alternatives like cache_params.max_connections and keeping the block, and Sentinel/HA for failover.
assertions: Does NOT recommend removing the coordination_redis block from config.yaml
Explains that REDIS_SOCKET_TIMEOUT does not take effect on the main Redis client (its constructor default wins), so it will not fix the stall
Explains that REDIS_CONNECTION_POOL_KWARGS is dropped and has no effect, pointing to a working knob such as cache_params.max_connections
Explains a risk of env-only coordination, such as a pod staying per-pod after a failed boot ping or losing the namespace prefix
Proposes an alternative path for failover stalls, such as keeping the explicit block and using Sentinel-based coordination or settings in the block itself
